description:
## Why this issue exists

Bearer tokens are issued in stoa-mail with an `expires_at` column in the `bearer_tokens` table, but it is not confirmed that every auth check path reads and enforces that column. An expired token that is still accepted is equivalent to no expiry.

All regulated frameworks (PCI-DSS, HIPAA, SOC2, NIST) require session/token expiry to be enforced, not merely stored.

## What needs to be done

- Audit every code path that validates a bearer token: JMAP API handler, admin API handler, any IMAP/SMTP credential path that uses tokens.
- Confirm `expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > NOW()` is part of the SQL query (not just a post-fetch check).
- Add an index on `(token_hash, expires_at)` if not present.
- Add a background task that periodically deletes expired tokens to prevent table bloat.
- Write a regression test: mint a token with a past expiry, attempt to use it, verify 401.

## Acceptance criteria

- Expired tokens are rejected at the database query level (not application-level post-fetch)
- A test with an expired token returns 401
- Tokens with no expiry are treated as indefinitely valid (existing behaviour preserved)
- Background cleanup runs and removes tokens expired > 24h

## Design notes

Regulatory refs: All frameworks. SOC2 CC6.1, PCI-DSS 8.2.9, NIST 800-63B.
title: Audit and enforce bearer token expiry
